tagline.text: A mixed-use estate in Pasig on the former Rizal provincial capitol grounds, with a mall and a park

children.text: Capitol Commons is a roughly 10-hectare mixed-use estate in Oranbo, Pasig, and an eastern extension of Ortigas Center. The upscale Estancia Mall, a large park and a dining strip sit side by side, so you can shop, eat and stroll in one outing.

Capitol Commons is a mixed-use development in Barangay Oranbo, Pasig City, Metro Manila. Often described as the eastern extension of Ortigas Center, it is bounded by Meralco Avenue to the west, Shaw Boulevard to the south, Camino Verde Road to the east and Capt. Henry Javier Street to the north. The estate covers about 10 hectares and is developed by Ortigas & Company. A shopping mall, office buildings, residential towers and a park share the site, so even in the middle of the city it feels fairly orderly and relaxed.

The name comes from the history of the site. The land was part of the Hacienda de Mandaloyon, which the family behind Ortigas & Company bought from the Augustinian order, and in 1950 the Rizal provincial capitol moved here and became the province's administrative center. The second capitol building served as the provincial seat from 1962 to 2009 and was demolished in 2010. After the Rizal provincial government moved to Antipolo, the land returned to Ortigas and has been redeveloped as a commercial estate since 2011. The neighborhood just to the south, Kapitolyo, is also named after the old capitol.
The heart of the estate is Estancia Mall. It is described as Pasig's first high-end shopping center, was completed in 2014, and its East Wing opened on
November 29

, 2019. The East Wing holds an SM Store, cinemas and a chapel. Capitol Commons Park, which takes up about half of the estate, adds open space for walking and resting that a mall alone cannot offer. If you are exploring the Ortigas area during a Manila trip, this is a calm place to eat and stroll away from the big malls.

In a word, this is a quiet urban outing. It is different from a day spent touring major sights, but the flow comes naturally: shop and catch a movie in the air-conditioned mall, walk the park around sunset, then have a drink at the dining strip in the evening. It is also a familiar spot for Koreans living in the Philippines for family meals and weekend outings, so it is a good way to feel local life even though guidebooks rarely mention it.

The centerpiece of the estate is a three-level upscale mall described as having about 30,000 sq m of leasable space. International and local brands are mixed together, and it is quieter than the other large malls in the Ortigas area, which makes for relaxed browsing. Tenants change often, so check official information before you go.

This open green space takes up roughly half of the estate. It has jogging paths and picnic spots, and many people walk their dogs here. Late afternoon, when the heat eases, is the most pleasant time, and there is little shade at midday, so bring a hat.

blocks.title: East Wing Cinemas and The Screening Room

children.text: The East Wing has cinemas operated together with SM Cinema, including halls with leather recliner seats and a private hall called The Screening Room with sofas and coffee tables. The Screening Room is said to be available for group and corporate bookings, so reserve ahead if you want to use it.

Ortigas Land has staged holiday light displays in the park at year-end. In 2021 it featured Christmas tree installations that double as benches, and in 2022 an Illuminated Path that ran every evening from
6 p.m.
to
. The schedule and design may differ this year, so check the official announcements.

Restaurants and pubs cluster around the mall, which makes it a good evening stop. Venues mentioned include the live-music venue 12 Monkeys Music Hall, The Perfect Pint with its house-brewed beer, and the gastropub Tipsy Pig. They are fine for a casual beer, but opening hours differ from place to place.

blocks.title: One Corner of the Ortigas Residential and Business District

children.text: The estate also has the North, South and West Wings of Estancia Offices and residential towers such as The Imperium and The Royalton. Office workers fill it on weekday afternoons and families on weekends, so the atmosphere changes with the time of day, which is part of the fun.

blocks.title: Pairing with the Kapitolyo Food Scene

children.text: Kapitolyo, just to the south, is known as a neighborhood of restaurants and cafes popular with young Filipinos. You only need to cross Shaw Boulevard, so it is easy to have lunch at the mall and dinner in Kapitolyo.

items.title: Half-Day Course
items.subtitle: From lunch to a park walk and dinner

children.text: Arrive at Estancia Mall and look around the main building. Browse the snacks at the basement supermarket and take your time wandering the stores.
Have lunch at a restaurant in the mall or nearby. Choices include Filipino, Japanese and Italian food.
Watch a movie at the East Wing cinemas, or rest in a cafe to escape the heat.
As the sun lowers, walk a loop of Capitol Commons Park. The lawns and paths are good for photos.
Eat dinner at the dining strip around the mall, and if you like, enjoy live music at a pub before heading home by Grab.
Movie times and store hours differ from day to day, so check on the day.
Start at Shangri-La Plaza on Shaw Boulevard and shop in the morning.
Take a Grab or taxi to Capitol Commons and have lunch.
Look around Estancia Mall and the park.
Cross over to Kapitolyo for dinner and dessert, then return to your hotel.
Travel takes longer during heavy traffic.

items.title: Taxi or Grab from Manila Airport

children.text: The travel time from Ninoy Aquino International Airport (MNL) to the estate varies a lot with traffic. It is best to avoid rush hours, and confirm the exact time locally.
Tell the driver Estancia Mall or Capitol Commons as your destination. If you book through an app, you can check the entrance point on the map.

items.title: MRT-3 and a transfer from central Manila

children.text: MRT-3 Shaw Boulevard Station is about
1 km
west of the estate. From the station, transfer to a jeepney, UV Express or Grab.
Passengers coming north from the Ayala Station area can ride to Shaw Boulevard Station without transferring. Check the latest announcements for operating hours and fares.

From BGC, a UV Express from the Market! Market! terminal or a Grab is the simplest option. From Quezon City, take a bus or jeepney along Ortigas Avenue to the Meralco Avenue intersection, then make a short transfer.
Public transport thins out at night, so a Grab is recommended.

The mall has several basement parking levels, and parking near the East Wing or main building elevators cuts your walking distance. Cars are reported at about ₱50 for the first 3–4 hours and about ₱20 per hour after, but rates may change, so confirm them and any discount rules locally.
The Shaw Boulevard end of Meralco Avenue has been closed since October 2022 for subway construction, and the closure is planned to last until 2028. Check a map app for current access roads.

With the mall and cinemas as the core, you can visit any time of year, but the November–May dry season is best for walking in the park. December to February in particular has cooler mornings and evenings that suit outdoor activities.

In March to May, daytime temperatures are high, so rest inside the mall at midday and head to the park around sunset. During the June–October rainy season, showers are frequent, so plan around the mall and cinemas instead of the park.
Light displays at year-end can make the estate busier than usual. For relaxed photos, aim for weekday evenings, and book weekend dinners to be safe.

Ortigas Center, close to the estate, has hotels such as Marco Polo, The Linden Suites and Richmonde Hotel, so it is easy to fit this outing into a day trip from there. Room rates vary a lot by season, so check booking sites.

Dining choices inside and around the mall are wide. Mentioned places include the modern Filipino restaurant Manam, Coco Ichibanya curry, a restaurant serving xiao long bao, and an Italian restaurant suited to large family meals. Shops change often, so check that the one you want is still open. For Korean food, you will have an easier time looking around Ortigas and Kapitolyo separately.
If you want a drink in the evening, pubs and lounges in the estate are a few minutes apart on foot. Most are reported to accept cards and e-wallets, but carry a little cash as well.
Weekday mornings and early afternoons are quiet, so you can see the mall and park at a relaxed pace.
The park is most pleasant around sunset, so plan to arrive in the late afternoon.
Check movie times on the app or on site first, and reserve The Screening Room in advance.
The mall is reported to be pet-friendly, so check the rules first if you bring a pet.
Make sure taxis use the meter, and use a ride-hailing app when possible.
The air conditioning inside the mall is strong, so bring a light jacket.
Check the official Ortigas Land channels for the year-end light display schedule.
Combining this with the Kapitolyo dining area just to the south widens your choice of where to eat.
Part of Meralco Avenue is closed for subway construction and car access can be inconvenient, so check a map app before you go.
Watch for pickpockets on crowded public transport and inside the mall, and carry your bag in front.

Hours are generally reported as about 10 a.m. to 10 p.m., and the open days of Holy Week 2026 used the same hours, but they vary by shop and holiday (the mall was closed on Maundy Thursday and Good Friday), so check.
Pubs and live venues stay open late, and hours differ by venue, so check before you go.
Roads around the estate may change because of construction. Re-check the pickup and drop-off point in your ride-hailing app.
Year-end events and the tenant mix change from year to year.
The business and commercial district the estate belongs to, packed with tall buildings and large malls. A short Grab ride makes it easy to combine into a full-day plan.
The city that contains the estate, which can be combined with other sights such as the Pasig River Esplanade. Travel times depend on traffic.
A leading mall on the Shaw Boulevard side, directly connected to an MRT station and easy to pair with this outing.
A large mall nearby along EDSA with a wide range of cinemas, restaurants and brand stores.
The neighborhood south of the estate, full of restaurants and cafes popular with young people. You only need to cross Shaw Boulevard, so it pairs well for a meal.
